name: Connected Vehicle & V2X Security
description: Security assessment of a vehicle's external interfaces and connected ecosystem. Covers the telematics control unit and its cellular, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth attack surface, remote service APIs and companion mobile applications, and the infotainment boundary; keyless entry and immobiliser systems, including rolling-code RKE, passive entry relay attacks, transponder cryptography and UWB-based digital key (CCC Digital Key); V2X communication under IEEE 1609.2 and ETSI ITS-G5 or C-V2X PC5, with pseudonym certificate handling and misbehaviour detection; and EV charging interfaces including ISO 15118 Plug and Charge, contract certificate provisioning, and OCPP charge-point backends. In-vehicle buses belong to ICSIOT-AUTO-IVN and diagnostics to ICSIOT-AUTO-ECU; generic IoT backends belong to ICSIOT-IOT-CLOUD; raw RF capture and demodulation belong to the WSEC domain; companion app internals belong to SWSEC-MOB-ANDROID and SWSEC-MOB-IOS.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to connected vehicle or V2X security

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands a vehicle's external interfaces and why connectivity extends the attack surface
evidence: Can name the external interfaces of a modern vehicle (cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, RKE, UWB, charging, V2X) and what each reaches
Can explain why a relay attack defeats passive keyless entry without breaking any cryptography
Understands the role of the telematics unit as a bridge between the internet and in-vehicle networks
Can describe what a V2X pseudonym certificate is for

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Enumerates and tests connected interfaces on a bench or test vehicle under supervision
evidence: Maps the exposed services of a telematics unit and infotainment head unit under guidance
Captures and replays RKE transmissions on a test vehicle or bench key using an SDR under supervision
Exercises remote service APIs and the companion app against a lab account, following a documented scope
Documents interface inventory, radio parameters and observed protocol behaviour

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses a vehicle's connected interfaces against a defined scope
evidence: Assesses remote service APIs for broken object-level authorisation, allowing one account to reach another vehicle
Demonstrates and bounds keyless entry weaknesses: rolling-code replay or desynchronisation, relay attacks, and weak transponder ciphers
Evaluates the telematics unit's separation from safety-relevant in-vehicle domains and whether a compromised TCU reaches them
Assesses ISO 15118 Plug and Charge contract certificate handling and OCPP backend authentication and authorisation
Reviews V2X message signing and verification, certificate validity handling and replay protection
Plans and documents testing so that radio transmission stays within legal limits and safety functions are only exercised on benches or immobilised vehicles

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Assesses complex connected architectures and their cryptographic protections; mentors others
evidence: Assesses UWB digital key implementations including distance-bounding and ranging integrity against relay and distance-reduction attacks
Evaluates V2X pseudonym certificate provisioning, SCMS or equivalent PKI enrolment, revocation and misbehaviour reporting
Builds custom tooling or test harnesses for proprietary telematics, keyless or charging protocols
Chains a connectivity foothold through to in-vehicle network or diagnostic impact as a demonstrated end-to-end attack path
Mentors staff on connected vehicle methodology, radio-legal test practice and responsible disclosure with manufacturers

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines the lab's connected vehicle assessment methodology; recognised authority
evidence: Authored the lab's connected vehicle and V2X assessment methodology, including its radio and safety rules
Published research or disclosed vulnerabilities in telematics platforms, keyless entry systems, V2X stacks or charging infrastructure
Advises manufacturers, suppliers or charging operators on connected architecture and PKI strategy
Contributes to automotive connectivity, V2X or charging security standards and industry working groups

assessment_methods.description: On a test vehicle and bench setup, inventory the external interfaces, demonstrate a relay or replay attack against keyless entry, and determine whether the telematics unit can reach a safety-relevant domain
Given a connected vehicle architecture and its remote API documentation, identify the paths by which an attacker holding only a user account could affect a vehicle they do not own
Review a connected vehicle assessment report for interface coverage, legality and safety of the test approach, and accuracy of impact and exploitability statements

equipment: Software-defined radio covering automotive RKE bands (315/433/868 MHz) with transmit capability
Shielded enclosure or RF-screened room for lawful transmission testing
ISO 15118 / CCS charging test equipment or EV charging emulator
Test vehicle or telematics bench unit with lab SIM and lab backend account
